name: com.businessratechecker/mcp
title: BusinessRateChecker
description: Business rates data for England and Wales: rateable values, comparables, verdicts, tribunal cases

tools.name: find_properties
tools.description: Search the 2026 rating list for England and Wales. Give a full postcode (e.g. 'WR3 8TJ') or an outward code (e.g. 'WR3'), optionally narrowed by words from the address or the description (e.g. 'unit 96a', 'cafe'), or a council's ba_code. Returns up to 20 properties with property_id, address, description, rateable value and business name where known. One building can hold many separate entries (floors, suites): ask which one if that matters. Use the property_id with the other tools. Costs 1 credit.

postcode.description: Full postcode or outward code, e.g. 'BD13 3EL' or 'BD13'.

query.description: Words from the address or the VO description to narrow the results, e.g. 'unit 2' or 'cafe'.

ba_code.description: Council (billing authority) code, e.g. '1835' for Worcester. Use instead of postcode.

uarn.description: A UARN, instead of postcode or ba_code: returns every current entry it covers, England and Wales.

include.description: Optional extra sections for the answer. The ones available are listed in the response under settings.include_supported; anything else is ignored and listed in settings.ignored. Leave out unless the user asks for something the normal answer lacks.

options.description: Optional extra settings by name. The ones available are listed in the response under settings.options_supported; anything else is ignored and listed in settings.ignored.

tools.name: get_property

Costs 1 credit.

property_id.description: The property_id from find_properties (the Valuation Office assessment reference), or a UARN, 4 to 15 digits. A UARN that covers several entries returns them all.

tools.name: get_overpayment_verdict
tools.description: BusinessRateChecker's verdict on whether a property's rateable value looks high against comparable properties, exactly as on the website report: strong_case, worth_checking, no_obvious_issues, not_enough_evidence or needs_turnover (with the website's wording in label, and flagged as on the overpayment map), with a suggested rateable value and indicative annual saving where there is one (and, where transitional relief probably caps this year's bill, the saving after it), the confidence, the hedge text that must be relayed with any figure, and a scheme_check showing how the VO's own valuation scheme values similar-sized properties (a saving on a property that sits within its scheme's range is a weak case on rate alone). Pass sole_property=false for a ratepayer with other business properties (Small Business Rate Relief then does not apply) or true if this is their only one. Also carries everything the full report sets out: grounds (every finding with its evidence), checks (rateable value, floor area, allowances, reliefs), route (Check, Challenge, Tribunal), next_steps and track_record (how Checks, Challenges and tribunal appeals on this kind of property have gone, England and Wales). Same engine as the website report. Costs 5 credits (one verdict per property per day).

property_id.description: The property_id from find_properties (the Valuation Office assessment reference), or a UARN, 4 to 15 digits. A UARN that covers several entries returns them all.

sole_property.description: true if this is the ratepayer's only business property, false if they occupy others. Omit if unknown, then ask before quoting the Small Business Rate Relief figure.

Costs 5 credits.

tools.name: search_properties
tools.description: List business properties in an area that match filters, sorted the way the question asks. Area is required (postcode, sector, district or council). Filters: street, sector, property type words (e.g. 'shop', 'office', 'warehouse', 'hotel'), business or building name (e.g. 'Novotel'), rateable value range, verdict, minimum indicative annual saving, minimum floor area. Sorts: rateable value, saving, floor area, or rateable value per square metre (per-m² rankings use only properties of 25 m² or more by default, and office rankings leave out banks and betting shops). Returns up to 50 rows with property_id, address, names, use, rateable value, floor area and £ per m² (the main use's, the same figures as the verdict; total_floor_area_m2 is the whole property, and floor-area filters and sorts use the main-use area), rate_basis and the verdict (the same as the website report, with label and flagged) and saving (before small business rate relief and transitional relief). Costs 1 credit per property returned (minimum 1); results stop 250 rows deep.

postcode.description: A full postcode ('W6 8DR'), a postcode sector ('W6 8') or a district ('W6').

council.description: Council name or part of it, e.g. 'Hammersmith' or 'Leeds'. Use instead of postcode for a whole council.

ba_code.description: Council (billing authority) code, e.g. '5390'. Alternative to council.

name.description: Business or building name, or address words, e.g. 'Novotel'.

street.description: Street name, e.g. 'Commercial Road'. Matches the start of the street.

property_type.description: Words from the Valuation Office description, e.g. 'shop', 'office', 'warehouse', 'hotel', 'restaurant'. 'warehouse' does not include retail warehouses unless sector is retail.

sector.description: One of: car_parking_and_storage, healthcare, industrial_and_warehousing, leisure_and_hospitality, offices, other_specialist, retail. Broad sector. Use it with £ per m² sorts so the ranking compares like with like.

verdicts.description: One of: strong_case, worth_checking, no_obvious_issues, not_enough_evidence, needs_turnover. Only these verdicts (the website's): strong_case, worth_checking, no_obvious_issues, not_enough_evidence, needs_turnover; e.g. ['strong_case', 'worth_checking'] for flagged properties. (Older words are still accepted and translated.)

min_saving.description: Only properties whose indicative annual saving is at least this many pounds.

min_area.description: Only properties of at least this many m². Default 25 for £ per m² sorts; 0 switches the default off.

sort.description: One of: rateable_value_desc, rateable_value_asc, saving_desc, floor_area_desc, rate_per_m2_desc, rate_per_m2_asc, transitional_relief_desc, rv_rise_pct_desc, rv_rise_desc. Default rateable_value_desc. rate_per_m2_* only ranks properties measured in square metres.

limit.description: Rows to return, 1 to 50 (default 10). Each row costs 1 credit.

cursor.description: next_cursor from a previous call, for the next page.

uarn.description: A UARN, instead of an area: the entries it covers, with their verdicts. The other filters still apply.

include.description: Optional extra sections for the answer. The ones available are listed in the response under settings.include_supported; anything else is ignored and listed in settings.ignored. Leave out unless the user asks for something the normal answer lacks.

options.description: Optional extra settings by name. The ones available are listed in the response under settings.options_supported; anything else is ignored and listed in settings.ignored.

tools.name: area_breakdown
tools.description: Counts, totals and medians for the business properties in an area, grouped by street, sector, property_type, postcode_sector, postcode, verdict or council: number of properties, total and median rateable value, median £ per m² (with n_per_m2, how many properties it is based on: per-unit and trade-valued properties are left out), verdict counts (the website's five verdicts), flagged count and share (strong_case + worth_checking, as on the overpayment map) and total indicative annual saving. Area is required. Optional filters: sector, property type, rateable value range. Up to 50 groups, sortable. Costs 2 credits.

council.description: Council name or part of it, e.g. 'Hammersmith' or 'Leeds'. Use instead of postcode for a whole council.

tools.name: explain_business_rates
tools.description: Free, no sign-in. Plain-English reference for 2026/27 with official sources, for England (default) or Wales (country: wales): how a bill is worked out, the multipliers, small business rate relief, retail/hospitality/leisure (England) or food and drink hospitality relief (Wales), pubs, charitable, rural and empty property relief, transitional relief, allowances, how a Check, Challenge and Appeal work, the deadlines, and who to contact. The two countries have different topic lists: omit topic to list them for the chosen country. Also BusinessRateChecker's published news and analysis (topic news, then news:<slug>), Learn articles (learn, learn:<slug>), glossary (glossary, glossary:<term>) and FAQ (faq), the same text as the website.

topic.description: One of: overview, multipliers, small_business_rate_relief, retail_hospitality_leisure, pubs_and_live_music, charitable_relief, rural_relief, empty_property, transitional_relief, check_challenge_appeal, allowances, deadlines, contacts, wales, food_and_drink_hospitality, all, news, learn, glossary, faq. A topic id, or 'all'; news, learn and glossary list their items, then ask for one as news:<slug>, learn:<slug> or glossary:<term>. Omit to list the topics for the chosen country.

country.description: england (default) or wales. Use wales for a property whose country is W.

tools.name: get_overpayment_map
tools.description: Free, no sign-in. The figures on BusinessRateChecker's overpayment map for England and Wales (2026 rating lists): properties analysed, properties flagged by our checks as paying too much, % flagged, '1 in N', median annual claim per flagged property, and the national indicative saving a year. With no area: England and Wales, England and Wales separately, and the 10 councils with the highest and lowest % flagged (country narrows these to England or Wales). With council or ba_code: up to 10 matching councils, each with its rank out of 318 (and within its country). Properties at or below the small business rate relief level (rateable value 12,000 GBP England, 6,000 GBP Wales) count one third. Same figures as https://businessratechecker.com/intelligence/map and its CSV. Each council and national block also carries win_rates: the Valuation Office's own statistics on how many resolved Checks and Challenges cut the rateable value, per rating list (2017 England only, 2023, 2026).

country.description: england or wales. Rank councils within England or Wales only. Omit for both.

tools.name: search_tribunal_decisions
tools.description: Published decisions of the Valuation Tribunal for England (about 3,300, 2020 onwards) and the Valuation Tribunal for Wales (about 1,400, 2018 onwards) on business rates appeals; each decision carries its country. Filter by area (postcode or council, English or Welsh), a property (property_id from find_properties), sector, property type words, outcome (won or lost), the decisive ground, the firm that represented the ratepayer, rating list year and decision date. Returns a summary over every match (decisions, attended, won, win rate of attended cases, cases reduced, median reduction %, rateable value removed, the commonest decisive grounds) and the newest decisions with the original, proposed, VO-conceded and tribunal values, the reduction, the grounds, a short reason summary and the representing firm. Cash-machine appeals are left out unless sector=atm. Costs 2 credits.

postcode.description: A full postcode ('W6 8DR'), a postcode sector ('W6 8') or a district ('W6').

council.description: Council name or part of it, e.g. 'Hammersmith' or 'Leeds'. Use instead of postcode for a whole council.

ba_code.description: Council (billing authority) code, e.g. '5390'. Alternative to council.

property_id.description: Only decisions about this property (the property_id from find_properties).

sector.description: One of: retail, office, industrial, leisure_hospitality, healthcare, education, car_park, other, unknown, atm. The tribunal data's own sector grouping.

property_type.description: Words from the property description, e.g. 'warehouse', 'shop', 'office'.

outcome.description: One of: any, won, lost. won = allowed, allowed in part or agreed at the hearing; lost = everything else. Default any.

ground.description: One of: rental_evidence, tone_of_list_comparables, floor_area_measurement, zoning_layout, material_change_of_circumstances, physical_works_disturbance, repair_state_deletion, split_merger_hereditament, trade_receipts_fmt, valuation_method, effective_date, validity_of_proposal, quantum_allowance, relief_or_exemption, other. Only decisions argued on this ground.

firm.description: The firm that represented the ratepayer, e.g. 'Colliers'.

list_year.description: 2010, 2017, 2023 or 2026. The rating list the appeal was against.

from.description: Decisions on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

to.description: Decisions on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

limit.description: Decisions to list, 1 to 25 (default 10). The summary always covers every match.

tools.name: find_rating_surveyors
tools.description: Which surveying firms represent ratepayers in business rates appeals. Returns the 12-month league of firms at the Valuation Tribunals for England and Wales (cases, attended, won, win rate, typical reduction, councils, latest decision, website), or the firms matching a name. With an area (postcode or council) it also returns the firms that represented ratepayers at the tribunal there in the same 12 months, and rating firms from our directory with an office within 50 km (firm, size, nearest office, distance, website). Firms only; no individual is named. BusinessRateChecker does not recommend or endorse any firm. Costs 1 credit.

tools.name: get_area_statistics
tools.description: How the rateable values the Valuation Office AMENDED in one month moved, for one council (billing authority) by name or code, or a short list of every council (name, code, number amended, % change) if neither is given. Covers only the properties amended that month, not the whole council, and one month is never a trend: call it for several months to see a direction. Always read pct_change with n_amended, top1_share_pct and median_mover_pct; pct_change is null when not publishable, and rankable=false means do not rank the place against others. For £ per m², property counts or overpaid shares across a council, use area_breakdown instead. Costs 1 credit.
